angleRead.name: Luis Navarro
angleRead.text: I'm standing in Laurel with a gap I can see but can't yet name. The signal this cycle points at a civic hole — someone should be accountable for something in this neighborhood, and the council either has or hasn't done something about it. But I don't have the specifics yet. What I have is a name: Rosalind Young, a smoke shop owner who lives here. She's the one person the record ties to Laurel. So I start with her. I walk into her shop, buy a pack of gum I don't need, and ask what's been bothering her about the neighborhood lately. I don't lead with council or accountability — I let her talk. The gap is real, but I won't pretend I know its shape until someone who lives here tells me. My job i
